I'll read the council brief in full first, then follow it exactly.The packet ends mid-Appendix B; I’ll pull the rest of SPINE.md so the review covers the full 920-line engine.Next I’ll check how SKILL.md loads SPINE, and whether wiring/colors already live elsewhere — that decides whether the appendix split is safe.I’ll size the candidate sections in tokens so the cuts are numbers, not guesses.VERDICT
The appendix split is the right *kind* of move and the wrong *unit*: Appendix B is non-law; Appendix A is three different documents sharing a heading, and its notation is misfiled law. The whale is Part VI (about a third of the file); a council that only evicts A+B and goes home has done the easy 12% and left the poll tax in place. A rule that is not in the always-loaded file is a rule nobody follows — unless the core contains a halt-and-load gate as loud as Gate-0, in which case the monolith is an accident of accretion and should die.

Q1 THE APPENDIX SPLIT — **NO as a lump; YES once A is carved.** Appendix B out, entire. Appendix A recipes/paths out. Appendix A color map + act glyphs + meter-mark grammar stay (promote into Part VIII). Failure mode if you dump A whole: the first line of a summon already has to sign (🟡➤). An orchestrator that “knows it can check” will not check before that line; 🔴 will mean both reviewing and reject; meter marks will vanish from spend lines; SKILL.md’s stale v4.0 legend (it still thinks it supersedes v3.1 and that meter wraps are “not narrated on this trunk”) becomes the live law by default — a fork, which is how law dies. Failure mode if you keep CLI strings in the engine: they rot, and they contradict the currency rule (never state a model id from memory). Wiring is *know-you-can-check*; notation is *must-have-memorised*. Appendix B’s failure mode is repeating a proven croak (agy headless empty-output; Codex 78K-token “exploit” kill). That is real, and it is situational: gate the load, and leave two studs in the trunk (see CUT 2).

Q2 WHERE THE WEIGHT IS
   [CUT 1] Appendix B field notes (~735 tokens)
   ANCHOR:  When a run PROVES something new, it goes here
   WHY SAFE: trunk load-gate + two croak-studs in CUT 2; FIELD-NOTES.md already exists at repo root
   ACTION:  MOVE to on-demand (merge with FIELD-NOTES.md)

   [CUT 2] Appendix B — two studs that stay (~40 tokens kept, not a save)
   ANCHOR:  Headless dispatches must EMBED the evidence in the prompt
   ANCHOR:  Phrase adversarial-verify tickets to Codex in defect/QA vocabulary
   WHY SAFE: these are the load-bearing minimum of B; the rest is capability gossip
   ACTION:  COMPRESS to two trunk lines under Tickets: agy headless auto-denies tools — embed evidence; Codex verify tickets use defect/QA vocabulary, never attacker vocabulary. Then “load field-notes before any CLI fallback.”

   [CUT 3] Appendix A CLI recipes + this-box ledger path (~380 tokens)
   ANCHOR:  Codex (OpenAI) — bounded implementation of a clear spec
   WHY SAFE: Doctrine 6 already names the default ledger as project-relative `model-lineage-ledger.md`; Transport Law already legalizes CLI as fallback; Review dispatch already says “Which concrete model that is, is the shop's wiring”
   ACTION:  MOVE to on-demand (SPINE-WIRING.md). Trunk stud: never invent a `--model` string; load wiring before the first vendor call.

   [CUT 4] Appendix A notation/colors/meter grammar (~850 of A's 1,380)
   ANCHOR:  METER MARKS ARE MANDATORY ON ANY LINE THAT CAN
   WHY SAFE: it is not safe to move. Part VIII already claims “the vendor→color map (Appendix A).” SKILL.md duplicates this and is already behind (v4.0 vs v4.2).
   ACTION:  COMPRESS into Part VIII (house colors, 🔨 / 🔴-as-suffix / ⛔ / ➤-belongs-to-whoever-points, five meter glyphs). MOVE bloodline marks, STATES laundry-list, crew-tier 📝 exception, and combo cookbook with the wiring file.

   [CUT 5] Part VI plan-card posture playbooks (~1,350 tokens movable of ~2,100)
   ANCHOR:  What each posture DOES — defined SOLELY as choices
   ANCHOR:  When the support seat is thin or missing. The adversarial
   WHY SAFE: surviving trunk: the card exists and is three questions; the five levers; “The card is an INPUT, not a lever”; “Review coverage is NOT a lever”; currency rule (never a quota/price/tier from memory). Per-posture prose and the ENTRY/MINIMAL/NONE playbooks are how you spend *after* you already decided to route.
   ACTION:  MOVE to on-demand. Trunk load-gate: before fanning out, down-tiering, or soaking a second vendor, load the budget module. Improvising a posture from its name is banned.

   [CUT 6] Episode theater — SHOW credits + JPEG recipe (~320 tokens)
   ANCHOR:  the DATE is for the backend only. Front-facing
   ANCHOR:  When the boss drops a screenshot during an episode
   WHY SAFE: surviving trunk: every mission with real dispatches gets `episodes/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>/` as harvest source. Date-vs-name and ending-credits are CREW/SHOW. `~1280px` / quality ~70 / `.claude\uploads\` is Appendix-A-class wiring.
   ACTION:  MOVE credits/style to CREW/SHOW; MOVE JPEG recipe to wiring; keep the folder rule.

   [CUT 7] THE COUNCIL procedure body (~450 tokens)
   ANCHOR:  Consent gates the convening — offered, never auto-fired
   WHY SAFE: Part I §2, Doctrine 5, and the fleet test already own consent, right-size, and the cap. Surviving trunk: council is the SPECIAL move; propose cost; dispatch only on explicit go; distinct lenses; attributed synthesis; boss rules. The six-step script is how you run one, not whether you may.
   ACTION:  MOVE procedure to on-demand. Convening from the summary is banned.

   [CUT 8] Doctrine 6 weekly review procedure (~220 tokens)
   ANCHOR:  THE WEEKLY LINEAGE REVIEW (the recalibration loop)
   WHY SAFE: surviving trunk: after a real dispatch, append an objective row; Facts ≠ Flavor; don’t bend work to feed the ledger. The STANDINGS/RECALIBRATE/HONESTY GATE ritual runs ~weekly, not per summon.
   ACTION:  MOVE to on-demand.

   [CUT 9] Restatements the morning pass missed (~700 tokens)
   ANCHOR:  The bench catches CODE bugs; the boss catches REALITY
   ANCHOR:  Who may review (the two legal paths, from Part IV's
   ANCHOR:  Operating mechanics for the principles. Higher tiers may
   ANCHOR:  when the reviewer can't read the repo, HAND IT
   ANCHOR:  Note on the block id: the v2026-07-22 r2 inside
   ANCHOR:  we don't have to make them deaf — just listen
   WHY SAFE: Ladder already owns gate 4; Part IV already owns who-may-review; the file header already owns “Neither CREW nor SHOW restates SPINE”; Review dispatch already owns stdin; Principle 9 already owns “Canonical text is defined once (Part VIII)”; Doctrine 4’s operative sentence is “a scope cut is a WIN celebrated, never a loss mourned.”
   ACTION:  COMPRESS D1.4 to a Part I §1 pointer. COMPRESS “Who may review” to “Part IV’s two legal paths” and keep only FIT routing. DELETE the Part VI opener blockquote. COMPRESS three-flips to “seat map is mission state; the only fixed point is Principle 3.” COMPRESS the block-id note to: block id tracks the invariant text, not SPINE’s version; do not retag it to match. MOVE the scalpel anecdote to SPINE-PROVENANCE.md.

   [CUT 10] Routing-ledger epistemology essay (folded into CUT 5’s ~1,350 if the whole plan-card block moves; ~200 if you only take this)
   ANCHOR:  It is an honesty aid, not proof: a model can
   WHY SAFE: surviving trunk: every dispatch writes one line with `default` and `changed?`; the ledger cannot prove causation.
   ACTION:  COMPRESS to those two sentences. MOVE “This project has never run that comparison. If you do, we will publish it” to provenance.

Q3 STRUCTURE — **restructure. The monolith is accretion. Part I was already titled “the engine in one frame” and then Parts II–VIII piled in.** Do not shrink to a 2k slogan card — that is how write-set containment and loop caps die. Three files, with load-gates that make compliance non-optional:

1. **SPINE.md (always loaded).** Target ~8–9k tokens. Contains: header + version + one-owner; Part I in full; Part II (doctrines, D2/D3/D5 already pointers); Part III principles + roles; Part IV fleet test (all seven conditions, not the stale “five,” plus lineage clause + anti-laundering + continuity); Part VIII invariant block byte-identical; ticket section names, write-set fence, worker statuses, escalation, capability-class table; the five levers named; “review coverage is NOT a lever”; currency rule; Reality Contract table; Amendment Law; the *locks* from the standalone laws (meter: readable or it doesn’t carry a lane; subsidy is never a foundation; spend needs a recorded allowance; probe the transport not the binary; fresh ≠ independent; reply-chain stays in lineage); panel/council consent lock; CUT 2 croak-studs; CUT 4 notation core. Plus the module law below.

2. **SPINE-MECHANICS.md (load-gated).** Adjudication full text (three lists, disputed-finding oracle, ranked ladder mechanized); review-dispatch FIT + reviewer-ticket four things; council six-step procedure; posture playbooks; Part VII review-culture + autonomous-hours; D6 weekly ritual; mission-report shape. Target ~5–6k.

3. **SPINE-WIRING.md (load-gated).** A’s CLI/overflow/ledger-path + B’s notes + JPEG recipe + bloodline/STATES cookbook. Target ~2k.

**MODULE LAW (this is the stud that makes the split honest):** When a named situation arises, HALT and read the named file before acting. Improvising from the trunk summary is banned — that is how law forks. Acting without the module is `REVIEW UNAVAILABLE` / mission incomplete, not a vibe. Gates: any delegated build or review → MECHANICS; any vendor call or seat-count → WIRING; any fan-out / down-tier / second-vendor soak → budget section of MECHANICS; any council → council section of MECHANICS.

What the core must contain so an orchestrator is honest *before* it has read anything else: Gate-0 (lean default; panels only on explicit go); Principle 3 + two legal paths + fail-closed unknown lineage; Ladder (never “it works”); fleet Declared/Bounded/Destined/Accounted/Governed/P3/inheritance; ambiguity is a finding; review coverage is not a lever; human merges; a metered seat must be readable; do not invent CLI strings or quota numbers. That is the first-move set. Everything else is how to do a kind of work correctly once you have decided to do that kind of work.

DEFENDED — what must NOT move, and why
- **Ladder of Truth, Gate-0, Reality Contract, Principle 3, Principle 6, Principle 8 units, Principle 10.** First moves. If they live in a module, the orchestrator builds first and reads later.
- **Fleet test including Destined and Governed** (Part I still says “all five hold” and names five; Part IV lists seven — repair the label, do not evict the two new prongs). Undeclared/uncapped/unlanded fleets are the original sin.
- **Three lists / containment** (`actual delta ⊆ write set` and `actual delta ⊆ review manifest`). Without it, independence of reviewer identity is theater; the builder chooses what is seen. May live in MECHANICS only if the load-gate fires before any review ticket is written.
- **“Fail CLOSED on the unknown”** and **solo-vendor-while-asleep = REVIEW UNAVAILABLE.** The cheap lie is counting a host banner as a vendor.
- **“Review coverage is NOT a lever.”** Cut this and SHOESTRING shops delete the channel. The whole budget chapter exists to protect that sentence.
- **Invariant block text** (not its biography). Principle 9: defined once, copied verbatim, sufficient to govern if the doctrine is never opened.
- **Amendment Law:** choose the form that leaves a trace. Meta-law for every later cut.
- **Meter Law cl. 4** (subsidy never a foundation) and **Council Seat Law cl. 1 vs 4 reconciliation.** Fresh scar, 2026-08-24. Moving it is how the contradiction returns.
- **Transport Law 2–4.** Fresh ≠ independent; reply-chain is lineage forever; `--version` is not a seat. Preflight is every summon (SKILL.md step 2); this is not on-demand.
- **Doctrines 2, 3, 4 as named reflexes.** They are already cheap. Deleting the name is how a stranger forgets the move. Evict the deaf-slot anecdote, not the scalpel.

TOTAL: **~4,200 tokens off a just-do-it / “what’s the job?” summon** if load-gates hold (CUT 1+3+5+6+7+8+9 ≈ 735+380+1350+320+450+220+700). **~1,500–2,000 off a typical one-builder-plus-one-reviewer summon** (wiring+notes+episode theater+council procedure+weekly ritual+restatement compress; posture and full adjudication come back). **~700–900 is real even on a full-rigor summon** (the compressions). Do not advertise 2,116 from a lumped A+B split: ~850 of that 2,116 is notation you must keep. Do not advertise 4,200 as a full-dispatch saving; that number is the death of the poll tax, not the death of the law. After this, SKILL.md’s ~4,048 tokens of restated notation/transport/meter is the next tax — out of scope here, but it is now 20%+ of every Deck summon and it is already forked from SPINE.

CONFIDENCE: **6.5/10.** Least sure cut: **CUT 5 (posture playbooks).** Routing *is* the orchestrator’s job; a SHOESTRING shop that fans out on WAR CHEST habits because it didn’t open the module is real money. That is the risky wall. What would change my mind: (1) evidence that models skip halt-and-load gates in practice — then keep the monolith and only do CUT 1, 3, 6, 9 (honest ~2,100, notation staying); (2) a token recount showing the plan-card block is much smaller than ~2,100; (3) the other two tier skills do not carry a color legend, which would make moving even the STATES cookbook more dangerous than I am treating it. I would not change my mind about Appendix B or about refusing to dump notation.
